title: Introduce token-bucket latency decomposer and fallback alert orchestrator
author: Aparna Rao
description: Context: We see intermittent long-tail latencies that spike under bursty admission patterns. Existing per-invocation metrics are useful but noisy: they surface total latency without splitting where time is spent (queueing, batching, execution, streaming). This PR adds a lightweight runtime instrument and downstream observability pipeline that decomposes per-invocation latency into token-bucket based phases and wires that decomposition into dashboards and an alert fallback orchestrator. Motivation: enable precise SLO attribution (which phase caused the tail) and automated alert attenuation + optional model fallback to preserve availability at acceptable cost.
commits: feat(obs): add token-bucket latency decomposer component; feat(metrics): expose phase-specific histograms and sparklines; feat(dashboards): add decomposed-per-invocation dashboard and tenant breakdown; feat(alerts): orchestrator to suppress noisy alerts and trigger fallback policy; fix(tests): coverage for decomposer edge cases; chore: docs and runbook updates
review_comments: Liam Chen (review): Overall nice separation of concern. Please ensure the decomposer doesn't spike cardinality: the proposal to hash callsite+route and emit a fixed-bucket label is good — prefer a 12-bit hash to avoid label explosion.

Author (Aparna): Switched to 12-bit route hash and added a sampling gate for low-volume tenants. See runtime/instrumentation/token_bucket_decomposer.rs + telemetry/metrics/registry.yaml for the sample config.
Sofia Mendes (review): The fallback orchestrator is powerful — need clear guardrails. Add a cooldown window and a maximum fallback rate per tenant to avoid oscillation.
Author (Aparna): Added cooldown and per-tenant rate limit (defaults in alerting/policies/fallback_orchestrator.yaml). Documented in runbook with recommended thresholds.
Noah Patel (approval): Verified metrics ingestion in staging and validated dashboard panels with synthetic replays. Approving pending CI green.
ci_summary: Checks: unit (pass), integration (pass on staging replay), lint (pass), observability-checks (pass after flakiness guard). One flaky test was fixed by adding deterministic timestamps to test fixtures.
testing_notes: Local unit tests + staging replay validated: 1) phase histograms align with synthetic stage (admission->batch->exec->stream) 2) KV-cache miss heat spikes map to execution phase 3) decomposed sparklines render with low overhead. Load test at 500 rps showed ~0.8% metric ingestion overhead and negligible path latency impact.
dashboard_notes: New dashboard 'Decomposed Invocation Latency' added with: per-route phase stacked histogram, per-tenant tail table (p95/p99 per-phase), sparklines for individual invocation cohorts, and cost-attribution panel correlating token counts with phase durations. Panel file: dashboards/observability/decomposed_latency.json
alerting_behavior: New orchestrator implements two behaviors: 1) alert attenuation: when noisy low-signal tenants cause frequent p99 flips, suppress alerts for a configurable quiet window and emit an advisory metric; 2) fallback activation: when execution-phase p99 exceeds threshold and queueing is not dominant, trigger model-fallback to a compatible lower-latency variant (rate-limited per tenant). All actions emit audit events and can be disabled per-tenant via policy.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated by runtime flag (off by default) 2) Canary: enable for internal org + 3 beta tenants for 48h with synthetic replay 3) Gradual ramp to 10% tenants over 72h while monitoring decomposition drift and alert noise 4) Full rollout after 1 week of stable metrics.
release_notes: Added token-bucket latency decomposition to give phase-level visibility (admission, batching, execution, streaming) and a new alert fallback orchestrator that can suppress noisy alerts and optionally trigger model fallbacks for high execution-phase tail. Configurable per-tenant. Backwards compatible; disabled by default.

notes_for_oncall: If you see repeated fallback activations for many tenants, first check the 'admission vs exec' phase distribution in the decomposed dashboard. If execution dominates and fallback rate limit is exhausted, rollback the orchestrator flag and open an incident for runtime performance. Audit logs are emitted under observability.audit.fallback.*
